rated_messages.input_message: Seeing other people smoke is a predictable and unavoidable trigger. Take 5 slow, deep breaths and remind yourself that the urge will pass and that you do not need to smoke.
Don't test yourself needlessly. If this social situation gets uncomfortable then leave briefly if you can. It really helps and it's fine to do it more than once!
Picture the people or things you care deeply about. On a scale of 0-10, how willing are you to let this urge pass for those reasons?

Read this rule out loud (if you can): IF someone offers me a cigarette THEN I will say 'no thanks, I don't want one.' Reading out if/then rules has been shown to help people stick with their decisions.
If you are tempted to smoke by being in this location, see if you can sit with that temptation for 1 minute. When the minute is over, do it again. Soon, it should pass.
What can you do right now to break the automatic habit of smoking to help you feel better? Pause. Close your eyes. And take 10 slow breaths.
When a craving hits, keep your hands busy by doing the dishes or taking out the trash. Small chores will help pass the time during a craving.
Crumple a piece of paper into a ball and imagine it is your urge. Toss the "urge" into the garbage or against the wall. By doing this, you are letting go of your urges.
Practice going 10 minutes without smoking. Think of it just as practice. When the urge passes, reward yourself with a break from work or dinner from your favorite restaurant!
If you miss doing something with your hands, try turning a coin or pen over and over with your fingers.
